rows.why: S1 answers four list questions: header (8), BOM (9), row order (1) and CRLF (10). Item 8 is closest because the scenario is mainly about the header row. Its pick matches the exact header text. Items 1, 9 and 10 also agree with S1.

The main thing S2 settles is how the Created date is written, which is item 7's question. Item 7 writes a full ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds, but S2 wants only the UTC date as YYYY-MM-DD. No item asks about status labels. Item 12 covers the missing-title part, which does agree.
Item 11 asks how an empty list is exported. Its pick returns the BOM and header line only, which is what S3 expects.

Item 12 asks how fields with commas, quotes or line breaks are handled. Its pick quotes only for comma, quote, CR or LF. S4 also requires quoting a title that starts or ends with a space, so the pick falls short.

No item's question asks about titles that start like a formula. Item 12's pick happens to say there is no formula-injection guard, which goes against S5. But item 12's question only covers missing titles and separator characters, and the instructions say to match on the question, not the pick.

Items 2-5 each cover one kind of bad requisition. Item 6 asks whether any bad record fails the whole export, which is the outcome S6 settles. Its pick throws and returns no CSV, so building fails. Item 6 doesn't say the error names the id, but items 2, 4 and 5 do.
